label: Déploiement du captage et stockage du carbone (CCS) pour l'industrie lourde d'ici 26 ans

sources: IPCC AR6 WGIII Ch.11 — Industrial CCS potential estimated at 3–4 GtCO2/yr by 2050; cement and steel are priority sectors
IEA CCUS in Clean Energy Transitions 2024 — Net-zero 2050 requires scaling from 50 MtCO2/yr (2024) to 7.6 GtCO2/yr
Global CCS Institute Status Report 2024 — 41 commercial CCS projects operational in 2024 capturing 49 MtCO2/yr
IPCC AR6 WGIII Ch.12 — CCS is the only available technology for deep decarbonisation of process emissions in cement and steel

planetary_limits.note: Geological CO2 storage requires monitoring for potential leakage over centuries

societal_indicators.note: CCS enables existing industrial workers to continue operations in decarbonised facilities
CCS requires 15–25% energy penalty, increasing energy demand of industrial processes

interactions.note: Carbon price of at least $80/tCO2 is required to make industrial CCS economically viable
Lower material throughput reduces the total scale of CCS deployment needed
Shared CCS infrastructure (pipelines, storage sites) reduces unit costs for both

methodological_note: Median impact of 3.5 GtCO2/yr calibrated against IPCC AR6 WGIII Ch.11 industrial CCS range of 3–4 GtCO2/yr by 2050. High uncertainty (score 3) reflects long implementation lag (7 years), dependence on $80/tCO2 carbon price prerequisite, and scaling challenge from current 50 MtCO2/yr to ~3500 MtCO2/yr. Pessimistic scenario models capture rate stagnation due to public opposition and geological storage constraints. Projection baseline: SSP2-4.5.
